_comment: A small set of worked examples, not an exhaustive roster. Each entry records what a `cbench gate` check found for that tag, and any configuration a run needed to produce valid data. Add your own entries as you gate-check new models. Tags must match exactly: a fork and its base are separate entries.
_where_your_own_entries_go: This file is the packaged, read-only seed. Do not edit it for your own models unless you are contributing a worked example back to the project. Your own gate-checked models belong in a separate local overlay file, found in this order: --registry-file, $OPENLLM_CBENCH_MODELS_FILE, the location pinned with `cbench config --set-models-file`, then ./models.json in the current directory. An overlay entry for a tag that also exists here replaces this seed entry outright; the two are not merged. `cbench gate --model <tag> --save` writes the overlay for you; see README.md, 'Populating it', for editing it by hand.

_schema.<exact-model-tag>: Object keyed by the exact string you pass to --model. It must match byte for byte, including any registry prefix (e.g. 'hf.co/org/repo:Q4_K_M'). A fork and its base model are two separate entries even if everything else about them matches.
_schema.architecture: String, from `ollama show <tag>` (Architecture), or your endpoint's equivalent. Read by the TUI Score screen's hardware fit warning.
_schema.params_b: Number: the parameter count in billions, always. No suite reads it, but the TUI's advisory VRAM fit warning does (core/hardware.py:check_model_fit, together with `quant`). `cbench gate --save` derives it from the endpoint's reported parameter_size: a 'B' value has its suffix removed, and an 'M' value (small models are reported in millions, e.g. '134.52M') is divided by 1000, so the unit never changes. A value that cannot be parsed is stored as the string 'unknown' rather than a guessed number, so anything reading this field must check that it got a number, not merely a truthy value.
_schema.quant: string, e.g. 'Q4_K_M'. No suite reads it; the TUI's advisory VRAM fit warning pairs it with `params_b` to pick a bytes-per-parameter estimate (core/hardware.py:BYTES_PER_PARAM), falling back to the Q4_K_M figure for an unrecognized string.
_schema.tools: Bool, informational only: whether the endpoint reported a tools capability for this tag at gate time. S1 and S3 need real tool calls, so a model without this capability cannot produce valid data for them.
_schema.thinking: Bool: whether the endpoint reported a thinking capability when `cbench gate` checked the model. True gives the model the larger automatic generation budget unless reasoning is switched off (core/budget.py).
_schema.thinking_mode: Optional string, acted on by the S2 channel suite. 'effort': the model exposes graded reasoning depth instead of a boolean toggle, so the suite runs an --effort all sweep instead of --think. 'ignores_think': the model disregards the API's think parameter and always reasons inline, so the suite runs --think false only and skips a pointless --think true sweep. Omit the key for an ordinary boolean think toggle; that is the default.
_schema.channel_separation: Optional object {think_on, think_off}, or null. Informational only: nothing reads this field itself, so if either state says anything other than 'clean', put the consequence in `caveats` too, which is the field the suites and `cbench gate` print. Typical values: 'clean', 'UNRELIABLE' (reasoning leaks into the visible answer at that think state), or a short explanatory string.
_schema.delimiters: Optional array of strings, acted on by the S2 channel suite and `cbench gate`. This model's own reasoning delimiters, for a model whose convention is not one of the four built-in families (<think>, [BEGIN FINAL RESPONSE], <|channel|>, <reasoning>). Write each the way you read it, with the opening and closing markers joined by an ellipsis, e.g. ["<odd>...</odd>"]. The two markers are matched separately, because a model emits the opening marker and then runs out of budget far more often than it emits the whole joined string. A hit is recorded as 'catalogued' in the CSV's merge_evidence column rather than attributed to a built-in family. The nested form {"reasoning": {"delimiters": [...]}} is also accepted and means the same. `cbench gate --save` does not write this field: add it by hand once you have confirmed the convention.
_schema.config_overrides: Object, acted on by every suite: the only field with a direct effect on a run. Recognised keys: num_ctx, num_predict, timeout, max_turns (S1 only), max_task_turns (S3 only) and think (S1 and S3). Each applies when the corresponding flag is not given on the command line; an explicit flag always wins. A gate check cannot derive good values for the budgets (for example, how much num_predict headroom a model needs), so add those by hand once a real run tells you. The one key `cbench gate --save` writes itself is think: false, when it finds the model only calls tools with its reasoning channel off.
_schema.caveats: Array of strings, printed verbatim in `cbench gate`'s report and in every suite's startup banner when this tag is used. Free text for a person to read before trusting a run, for example 'think=off is unreliable for this model' or 'this model ignores --think entirely'.

caveats: Exposes graded reasoning depth (low, medium, high) rather than a boolean toggle. The S2 suite reads thinking_mode from this catalogue and runs an --effort sweep for this tag by default.

At think=off, reasoning text goes into the visible answer behind an inline marker instead of a separate field, so every CLEAN or CHANNEL_LEAK verdict at think=off is unreliable for this model. think=on data is unaffected and citable.

At S1's default budgets (num_predict 2048, num_ctx 8192) this model can be cut off mid-turn on longer agentic tasks. Raise num_ctx above num_predict by a real margin, not num_predict alone; otherwise a mid-turn truncation can look like stochastic derailment.

This model ignores the API's `think` parameter and always reasons inline before any tool call (confirmed with a raw chat-endpoint check). The S2 suite reads thinking_mode from this catalogue and does not sweep --think for this tag. The only lever that helps is the raised num_predict above, so that the reasoning pass does not exhaust the budget before a tool call.

Even at a raised num_predict, some tasks may produce tool activity with no final answer, and at least one task pattern may produce no tool calls whatever the budget. Read the transcripts rather than assume one fix covers every task.

If you gate-check a community fork of this model, diff its Modelfile sampling parameters against the base explicitly, not just architecture, quant and capabilities. A Modelfile parameter set on one arm and not the other (a repetition or presence penalty, for example) confounds any base-versus-fork comparison without showing up in a capability check. Every suite pins presence_penalty to 0 for this reason; check for any other parameter a Modelfile might set.

The endpoint does not report a tools capability, and S1 and S3 need real tool calling, so they will not produce valid data. gemma3 (distinct from gemma4, which is also in this catalogue) does not expose tool calling through this endpoint.
The endpoint does not report a tools capability, and S1 and S3 need real tool calling, so they will not produce valid data.

The endpoint reports a tools capability, but the tool-call round trip failed: no tool_calls block came back for a trivial single-tool prompt. That is a subtler failure than having no tools capability at all. has_tools_capability=true is not sufficient evidence that a model will produce a usable tool call; always check the gate's tool-call line as well as the capability list.
The same pattern as qwen2.5-coder:14b: the endpoint reports a tools capability but the round trip fails. Do not treat this model as tool-calling-capable for S1 or S3 despite its capability list.

This model's Modelfile stop token contains a non-ASCII special-token character (U+FF5C, '｜', part of its <｜User｜>-style markers). A model's own special tokens are a real source of non-ASCII text, not only multilingual output; core/console.py configures UTF-8 output so that printing them cannot crash a Windows console.

No reasoning channel by design. It shares its architecture family with granite4.2:8b, but this generation does not expose 'thinking' at all, so S2 has nothing to sweep for this tag. S1 and S3 are unaffected.

Community safety-ablated fork of granite4.1:8b (also in this catalogue). It matched the base on architecture, parameters, quant and capabilities at gate time. Diff the Modelfile sampling parameters explicitly before treating any base-versus-fork comparison as clean (see the qwen3.5:9b caveat for why).

Community safety-ablated fork of gpt-oss:20b (also in this catalogue). `ollama show` reports a different quant label for this fork (F16) than for its base (MXFP4). This entry has not checked at the tensor level whether that is a real precision difference or a labelling artefact of which weight subset `ollama show` reports, so treat the mismatch as something to check before citing any base-versus-fork comparison, not as settled either way.
Exposes graded reasoning effort (low, medium, high) rather than a boolean think toggle, like its base. This catalogue's thinking_mode field routes the S2 suite to an --effort sweep for this tag.

Community safety-ablated fork of gemma4:12b (also in this catalogue). It matched the base on architecture, quant and capabilities at gate time. Diff the Modelfile sampling parameters explicitly before treating any base-versus-fork comparison as clean.

Third-party distillation naming pattern ('empero'). core/provenance.py's provenance_note() labels this in every generated report as unaffiliated with the base model's original vendor; do not present its behaviour as a property of the Qwen model family without that qualifier.
No tools capability. S1 and S3 need real tool calling and will not produce valid data against this model.

Reasoning text leaks into the visible answer instead of a separate field at both think states (the gate's merge guard fired on both), so every S2 verdict against this model would be unreliable whatever the --think setting. In short, none of the three suites can currently assess this model validly. It is kept as a worked example of what a complete gate-check failure looks like, not as a model to run.

think=off gate content was unusually long (1500+ characters for a one-sentence prompt) with 0 reported thinking characters. That is consistent with this model marking its reasoning with a delimiter none of the built-in families recognise, so the automated 'clean' at think=off should not be taken at face value for this tag. Verify the delimiter by hand before citing any think=off S2 result for this model, and if you identify it, record it in this entry's `delimiters` field, which both `cbench gate` and the S2 suite read.

No tools capability and no thinking capability reported. S1 and S3 need real tool calling and will not produce valid data, and S2 has no reasoning channel to sweep. A capable-sounding 'deep' reasoning name is not evidence of either capability: always gate-check rather than infer from the tag.
